titles: Deep rot: On the Election Commission of India’s functioning during its SIR
Trading smart: On the India-New Zealand FTA

set_a.instruction: Directions: In the following sentence, one part may contain an error. Identify that part. If there is no error, choose No error.
set_a.sentence: In light of the growing public concern over the Special Intensive Revision, / the two dissenting Election Commissioners / just submitted their formal objections / to the unilateral decisions taken by the Chief.
options: In light of the growing public concern over the Special Intensive Revision,
to the unilateral decisions taken by the Chief.
set_a.explanation:
**Correction & Rule:**
Replace 'just submitted their formal objections' with 'have just submitted their formal objections'. In standard competitive exam English, the adverb 'just' (indicating an action completed a very short time ago) is used with the Present Perfect tense ('has/have + past participle') rather than the Simple Past tense to connect a recent action to the present context.

**Why other parts are correct:**
• 'In light of the growing public concern over the Special Intensive Revision,': This introductory prepositional phrase is grammatically sound and correctly establishes the present context.
• 'the two dissenting Election Commissioners': This is a grammatically correct plural noun phrase acting as the subject of the sentence.
• 'to the unilateral decisions taken by the Chief.': The preposition 'to' is the correct collocation after the noun 'objections' (objections to something), and the reduced relative clause 'taken by the Chief' properly modifies 'decisions'.

set_a.instruction: Directions: In the following sentence, one part may contain an error. Identify that part. If there is no error, choose No error.
set_a.sentence: The new application form was altered without the government amending the rules contained / unauthorised questions about the electoral roll of the last survey, / prompting the election commissioners to flag the centralisation of the database / and record that field officials lacked complete access to the portal.
options: The new application form was altered without the government amending the rules contained
unauthorised questions about the electoral roll of the last survey,
prompting the election commissioners to flag the centralisation of the database
and record that field officials lacked complete access to the portal.
set_a.correct_answer: The new application form was altered without the government amending the rules contained
set_a.explanation:
**Correction & Rule:**
Replace 'The new application form was altered' with 'The new application form that was altered' (or simply 'The new application form altered'). In relative clauses, a relative pronoun (such as 'that' or 'which') cannot be omitted when it functions as the subject of the relative clause; omitting it here results in a run-on structure with two competing main verbs ('was altered' and 'contained') for the same subject.

**Why other parts are correct:**
• 'unauthorised questions about the electoral roll of the last survey,': This part is grammatically correct, serving as the direct object of the verb 'contained' and followed by a standard prepositional phrase modifier.
• 'prompting the election commissioners to flag the centralisation of the database': This part correctly uses the participial phrase 'prompting...' to show the consequence of the main action, followed by a standard infinitive construction ('to flag').
• 'and record that field officials lacked complete access to the portal.': This part maintains perfect parallel structure with 'to flag' (the infinitive 'to' is elliptically omitted before 'record') and uses a grammatically sound noun clause in the past tense ('lacked') to match the timeline of the sentence.

set_a.instruction: Directions: In the following sentence, one part may contain an error. Identify that part. If there is no error, choose No error.
set_a.sentence: Following widespread concerns over software-generated discrepancies in the voter rolls, / the election commission has formulated a statutory audit process, / and the special oversight panel tasked with inspecting the central database / will hold its inaugural hearing next Monday as per the official schedule.
options: Following widespread concerns over software-generated discrepancies in the voter rolls,
the election commission has formulated a statutory audit process,
and the special oversight panel tasked with inspecting the central database
will hold its inaugural hearing next Monday as per the official schedule.
set_a.correct_answer: will hold its inaugural hearing next Monday as per the official schedule.
set_a.explanation:
**Correction & Rule:**
Replace 'will hold' with 'holds'. The simple present tense is used to denote an action that is part of a fixed timetable, official program, or scheduled future event.

**Why other parts are correct:**
• 'Following widespread concerns over software-generated discrepancies in the voter rolls,': This participial phrase correctly establishes the background context using appropriate prepositions ('over', 'in').
• 'the election commission has formulated a statutory audit process,': The present perfect tense ('has formulated') accurately indicates a recently completed official action that bears present relevance.
• 'and the special oversight panel tasked with inspecting the central database': The subject noun phrase is grammatically well-formed, with the past participial phrase ('tasked with inspecting...') correctly modifying 'panel'.

set_a.instruction: Directions: In the following sentence, one part may contain an error. Identify that part. If there is no error, choose No error.
set_a.sentence: Addressing the media on the pending voter list cases, Mr. Sandhu stated that / the tribunal may dismiss all such appeals / seeking to remove registered citizens / if no official authorization was presented.
options: Addressing the media on the pending voter list cases, Mr. Sandhu stated that
the tribunal may dismiss all such appeals
if no official authorization was presented.
set_a.correct_answer: the tribunal may dismiss all such appeals
set_a.explanation:
**Correction & Rule:**
Replace 'the tribunal may dismiss all such appeals' with 'the tribunal might dismiss all such appeals'. In reported speech, when the reporting verb is in the past tense ('stated'), the modal verb 'may' changes to 'might' to maintain correct tense harmony.

**Why other parts are correct:**
• 'Addressing the media on the pending voter list cases, Mr. Sandhu stated that': The introductory participial phrase correctly modifies 'Mr. Sandhu', and the reporting verb 'stated' correctly sets the past context.
• 'seeking to remove registered citizens': The participial phrase functions correctly as an adjective modifying 'appeals'.
• 'if no official authorization was presented.': The subordinate conditional clause maintains tense consistency with the past tense passive voice 'was presented'.

set_a.instruction: Directions: In the following sentence, one part may contain an error. Identify that part. If there is no error, choose No error.
set_a.sentence: A number of appeals filed against the arbitrary deletion of electors has been decided / in favour of the aggrieved citizens, / which strongly indicates that the summary revision exercise / had erroneously disenfranchised thousands of genuine voters.
options: A number of appeals filed against the arbitrary deletion of electors has been decided
in favour of the aggrieved citizens,
which strongly indicates that the summary revision exercise
had erroneously disenfranchised thousands of genuine voters.
set_a.correct_answer: A number of appeals filed against the arbitrary deletion of electors has been decided
set_a.explanation:
**Correction & Rule:**
Replace 'has been decided' with 'have been decided'. The phrase 'a number of' acts as an indefinite quantifier meaning 'several' or 'many' and takes a plural noun ('appeals') followed by a plural verb ('have been decided'), unlike 'the number of' which denotes a single specific figure and requires a singular verb.

**Why other parts are correct:**
• 'in favour of the aggrieved citizens,': This prepositional phrase correctly functions as an adverbial modifier describing how the appeals were decided, with proper adjective and noun usage.
• 'which strongly indicates that the summary revision exercise': The non-restrictive relative pronoun 'which' correctly refers to the preceding clause/situation, taking a singular verb 'indicates' followed by the conjunction 'that'.
• 'had erroneously disenfranchised thousands of genuine voters.': The past perfect tense 'had disenfranchised' correctly conveys an action completed prior to the subsequent restoration of electors, with the adverb 'erroneously' appropriately modifying the verb.

set_c.instruction: Directions: In the following sentence, a word has been omitted. Choose the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.
set_c.sentence: The apex court's uncritical endorsement of the summary revision protocol drew widespread criticism, primarily because transferring the burden of proving eligibility from the state to individual citizens is fundamentally ______ to the constitutional guarantee of universal adult suffrage.
set_c.explanation:
**Why 'antithetical' is correct:**
'Antithetical' means directly opposed or mutually incompatible. The sentence highlights that placing the burden of proving eligibility on citizens contradicts the democratic principle of universal adult suffrage, which requires the state to protect and facilitate voting rights. Hence, 'antithetical' fits the critical tone and contextual logic perfectly.

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'conducive': Means tending to promote or assist an outcome. Transferring the burden to citizens restricts voting rights and drew criticism, so it cannot be conducive to universal adult suffrage.
• 'subservient': Means excessively submissive or serving in an inferior capacity. It is typically used for individuals or subordinate roles, not for describing a systemic contradiction between a policy and a constitutional principle.
• 'analogous': Means comparable or similar in certain aspects. A regressive verification rule cannot be said to be similar to the guarantee of voting rights; rather, it directly conflicts with it.

set_c.instruction: Directions: In the following sentence, a word has been omitted. Choose the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.
set_c.sentence: Faced with widespread allegations of arbitrary voter disenfranchisement, civil rights groups have petitioned the apex court for an immediate ______ on any further revisions to the database until an independent forensic audit is concluded.
set_c.explanation:
**Why 'moratorium' is correct:**
'Moratorium' means a temporary prohibition or suspension of an ongoing activity. In the given editorial context, the petitioners are asking the court to temporarily halt or freeze all further revisions until an audit is completed, making 'moratorium on' the most precise and appropriate fit both contextually and collocationally.

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'concession': Refers to a thing granted or yielded in response to demands; one cannot place an 'immediate concession on revisions' to halt a process.
• 'stipulation': Means a specified condition or requirement demanded as part of an agreement. It does not denote an official temporary freeze or suspension of an activity.
• 'prerogative': Means an exclusive right or privilege belonging to a particular individual or official body, which makes no sense in the context of halting database deletions.

set_c.instruction: Directions: In the following sentence, a word has been omitted. Choose the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.
set_c.sentence: Faced with mounting pressure from political parties and the media over alleged discrepancies in the voter list, the Election Commission of India ordered a Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, a corrective measure aimed primarily at ______ public anxieties regarding the integrity of the democratic exercise.
set_c.explanation:
**Why 'allaying' is correct:**
'Allay' means to diminish, soothe, or alleviate fear, suspicion, or worry. In the context of the sentence, the Election Commission's corrective measure (the Special Intensive Revision) is designed to soothe or reduce the public's anxieties regarding the election's integrity. 'Allaying anxieties' is a highly standard English collocation.

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'redressing': While 'redress' means to remedy or set right an undesirable situation, it collocates with words like 'grievances', 'wrongs', or 'imbalances'. One cannot 'redress anxieties'.
• 'harboring': 'Harbor' means to keep a thought or feeling (typically a negative one) in one's mind. A corrective measure by a public institution would aim to eliminate or resolve public anxieties, not harbor (keep/shelter) them.
• 'instigating': 'Instigate' means to initiate, provoke, or incite an action or event (usually something negative, like a riot or rebellion). It is contextually opposite to what a corrective measure aims to do to anxieties.

set_c.instruction: Directions: In the following sentence, two words have been omitted. Choose the most appropriate pair of words to fill in the blanks.
set_c.sentence: While the projected doubling of trade by 2030 may seem ______ from a macroeconomic standpoint, the policy's real-world implications are ______ for the survival of millions of small-scale enterprises.
set_c.explanation:
Why 'paltry, critical' is correct:
'Paltry' means petty, meager, or insignificantly small, which perfectly captures the idea that a doubling of trade is still a 'minuscule amount' on a macroeconomic scale. 'Critical' means of decisive importance or crucial, which fits the context that these trade policies are vital for the survival of livelihood-generating small businesses. Together, they establish the perfect contrast introduced by the conjunction 'While'.

Why other options are incorrect:
• 'nominal, redundant': While 'nominal' (insignificant or existing in name only) fits the first blank, 'redundant' (superfluous or no longer needed) contradicts the logic of the sentence, as trade cannot be redundant for the survival of businesses.
• 'formidable, negligible': This pair reverses the logic of the sentence. 'Formidable' (inspiring respect through size or power) contradicts the premise that the trade volume is minuscule, and 'negligible' (insignificant) incorrectly suggests that the implications do not matter for the survival of small businesses.
• 'profound, incidental': 'Profound' (very great or intense) contradicts the idea of a small or minuscule macroeconomic starting point, while 'incidental' (occurring merely by chance or as a minor accompaniment) downplays the crucial impact on livelihoods, which is the main focus of the sentence.

set_c.instruction: Directions: In the following sentence, two words have been omitted. Choose the most appropriate pair of words to fill in the blanks.
set_c.sentence: As unilateral tariff hikes and maritime chokepoints threaten to ______ global supply chains, Indian exporters need decisive policy support to ______ alternative overseas markets before their margins erode entirely.
set_c.explanation:
**Why 'hamper, penetrate' is correct:**
'Hamper' means to hinder or impede the progress of something, accurately describing the adverse impact of tariff hikes and maritime bottlenecks on trade flows. 'Penetrate' means to successfully enter or establish a presence in a commercial market, forming a standard business collocation ('penetrate alternative markets') that completes the logic of exporters seeking new trade routes to protect their profitability.

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'jeopardize, forfeit': While 'jeopardize' (endanger) logically fits the first blank, 'forfeit' means to surrender or lose something as a penalty, which completely reverses the contextual logic of seeking support to enter new markets.
• 'invigorate, explore': While 'explore' fits the second blank contextually, 'invigorate' means to strengthen or revitalize, which logically contradicts the disruptive threat posed by tariffs and chokepoints.
• 'stabilize, secure': While 'secure' fits the second blank well, 'stabilize' means to make steady, which creates a logical contradiction when paired with the negative threats of trade disruptions.
